question: What kind of organism causes amoebiasis?
explanation: Spot on! Amoebiasis is caused by a tiny, single-celled protozoan parasite. You've got this! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h1)

question: Why is poor sanitation a major risk factor for catching amoebiasis?

options.A: Lack of clean water triggers a genetic predisposition to the disease
options.B: Poor waste management makes the air toxic to human lungs
options.C: Sanitation issues increase exposure to contaminated food and water
options.D: Inadequate hygiene causes spontaneous mutations in human cells

explanation: Exactly! The parasite travels through the fecal-oral route, so clean food and water are your best defense. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h1)

question: What is the specific name of the parasite responsible for amoebiasis?
explanation: Well done! *Entamoeba histolytica* is the classic culprit behind human amoebiasis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h2)

question: Which form of this parasite helps it survive harsh conditions outside the human body?
explanation: Correct! Cysts have a tough outer wall that lets them survive in contaminated soil or water for weeks. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h2)

question: What distinct shape do the ulcers formed by this parasite in the colon usually take?
explanation: You got it! As the parasites burrow into the gut lining, they carve out classic flask-shaped sores. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h3)

question: A patient comes in with right upper quadrant belly pain, fever, and a history of dysentery. What condition should you suspect?
explanation: Spot on! When the parasites travel up into the liver via the bloodstream, they can form a painful, pus-filled abscess. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h3)

question: Why do doctors often ask for multiple stool samples when testing for intestinal parasites?

options.A: Laboratories require a large bulk sample for chemical mixing
options.B: Single samples automatically get lost during transport
options.C: Parasites are not always shed continuously in every stool
options.D: Infection levels change every single hour of the day

explanation: That's right! Because the parasite isn't passed out in every single bowel movement, checking samples over a few days boosts your chances of catching it. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h4)

question: Which diagnostic test is best when checking for a suspected amoebic liver abscess?
explanation: Correct! Imaging like an ultrasound gives a clear view of the liver to spot any fluid or abscesses. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h4)

question: Which medication is commonly given to kill active parasites hiding in body tissues?
explanation: Spot on! Metronidazole is the go-to drug for wiping out active, tissue-invading amoebas. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h5)

question: Why is a luminal medication also prescribed along with tissue-active drugs?

options.A: To replace lost electrolytes and boost red blood cell production
options.B: To permanently numb the lining of the stomach against acid
options.C: To speed up the healing of skin lesions on the abdomen
options.D: To clear remaining cysts from the bowel lumen and prevent relapse

explanation: Exactly! While one drug clears the tissues, the luminal agent mops up any cysts left in the gut so the infection doesn't bounce back. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h5)

question: What severe complication happens when an intestinal ulcer eats all the way through the bowel wall?
explanation: You nailed it! A break through the entire bowel wall is called a perforation—definitely a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h6)

question: A patient with severe amoebiasis suddenly gets a rigid, board-like tummy and severe pain all over. What is your primary worry as a nurse?
explanation: Spot on! A rigid abdomen is a classic red flag for peritonitis caused by a perforated bowel. Quick action is life-saving! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h6)

question: What is the single most important personal habit for preventing amoebiasis?

options.A: Wearing protective gloves in public places
options.B: Meticulous handwashing with soap and water
options.C: Avoiding all forms of physical exercise

explanation: Correct! Good old soap and water wash away cysts and break the cycle of transmission. Simple yet powerful! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h7)

question: Which of these methods is NOT a reliable way to make water safe from amoebic cysts?

options.A: Boiling the water vigorously for at least one minute
options.B: Allowing the water to settle in a dark container for an hour
options.D: Filtering the water through a fine membrane filter

explanation: You got it! Letting water settle just drops heavy dirt—it doesn't kill microscopic cysts. Always boil, filter, or treat chemically! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h7)
